protected_integrity_finding._note: Reported separately from the F65 score, per the dispatch instruction.
protected_integrity_finding.verdict: A defect in the ticket's lifetime and recovery-target rules, NOT INV-14 working as designed.
reasoning: The design intent is stated in protected-integrity.sh itself and treats this outcome as the bug it was fixing: '심사를 통과한 편집이 매번 복구됐다' and '편집 → 검증 → 커밋이라는 하네스 자신의 워크플로우가 성립하지 않는 상태였다'. A reviewed edit being reverted is the declared failure mode, not the intent.

The recovery TARGET is HEAD, not the most recently ticketed content. So a single unticketed edit discards an unbounded amount of previously reviewed, uncommitted work on that file -- which is what happened (step 17 and 18 edits lost together, quarantined at 2026-09-12T23:27:51Z = 9/13 08:27 KST, recovered by hand in 820e6da at 08:46 KST). The blast radius is the file, and it is maximal by construction.

The ticket is minted from NEW_CONTENT (the PreToolUse PREDICTION of post-edit content) hashed with `printf '%s'`, while verification hashes the on-disk file via `printf '%s' "$(cat …)"`, which strips ALL trailing newlines rather than one. Any edit shape where the prediction and the write differ -- or where invariant-guard exits before NEW_CONTENT is set, which its own comment documents as a real branch -- silently yields no ticket, and the next Bash call reverts.

The ledger is not garbage-collected for paths outside PROTECTED_GLOBS. `consume_ticket` is only reached from the loop over `git ls-tree` paths filtered by PROTECTED_GLOBS, so tickets for any other path accumulate forever. Measured: progress/.guarded-edits is 2058 lines, of which 1783 are for bare `settings.json` (not in PROTECTED_GLOBS) plus ~70 for `.tmp/**` and `.claude/worktrees/**` test/worktree paths. The code comment claims this pollution class was closed after it reached 209 lines; it is now 10x that.
minimal_fix_direction: Restore to the most recent ticketed content for that path when one exists, falling back to HEAD only when none does. This keeps detection identical while cutting the blast radius from 'all uncommitted work on the file' to 'the one unreviewed edit'. Requires storing the ticketed blob (git hash-object -w) alongside the sha, which the ticket already is.

Garbage-collect the ledger: consume or expire ticket lines whose path is not in PROTECTED_GLOBS, and refuse to mint a ticket when the derived root is not the real repository root (the existing `$file_phys == $root/*` check passes when root itself is a temp lab).
Treat a mint failure as loud, not silent: if a protected file is edited and no ticket results, say so at edit time rather than reverting at the next Bash call.
protected_integrity_finding.severity: high for harness usability and for trust in the control (an operator who loses work twice starts editing protected files through channels the detector does not watch); low for the security property itself, since quarantine preserves content and detection is unaffected.
